title: Birthdays Around the World
strapline: Everyone has a birthday — but ear-pulling in Brazil, red eggs in China, a piñata in Mexico? Let's find out how the world says 'happy birthday'.
intent: A birthday is the one celebration every single child shares, which makes it the perfect, most inclusive way to explore how different families and countries mark the same happy day in their own special ways.
Discovering different birthday customs — foods, games, songs, traditions — grows knowledge of the wider world and genuine respect for difference.
Every child gets to feel special and seen — their own birthday, their own family's way of celebrating, honoured alongside everyone else's.
Birthdays are bursting with mathematics — counting candles, adding a year, one party hat for each guest, sharing the cake fairly, how old and how many.
Making cards, invitations and lists gives writing a real and joyful job.
Rich language and comparison flow in — birthday, candle, older, celebrate, tradition, wish, party, share.
implementation: Explore how birthdays are celebrated in different countries and families — invite families to share their own customs so it stays real, accurate and inclusive.
Set up a birthday role-play — party table, cake with candles, hats, presents, cards — and let children host their own celebrations.
Model the counting and comparing: 'How many candles this year? One more than last year! I wonder how your family celebrates birthdays at home.'
Bring in maths naturally — count and add candles, match a hat and plate to each guest, share the cake into fair pieces, order who is oldest.
Try a few different traditions with joy and respect — a song in another language, a piñata, a special food — always led by the families who know them.
Make cards, invitations and birthday lists so writing has a purpose, and celebrate each child's own real birthday warmly through the year.
key_questions: How many candles this year? How many was it last year?
How does your family celebrate birthdays at home?
Have we got a hat and a plate for every guest?
How could we share this cake so everyone gets a fair piece?
Who is the oldest here — how could we find out?

impact.text: Children learn that families and countries celebrate the same happy day in many different, welcome ways.
Children count candles, add a year and match a hat and plate to each guest.
Children share the cake fairly and work out how old and how many.
Children make cards, invitations and lists, giving writing a real and joyful job.
Every child feels special and seen as their own birthday and family's customs are honoured.

enhancements: A birthday role-play table with cake, candles, hats, presents and cards to host celebrations.
Families invited to share their own birthday customs — a song, a food, a tradition.
Try a piñata, red eggs or a birthday song in another language, always led by the families who know them.
A 'how old are you' ordering line, youngest to oldest, using the children's real ages.
A rolling birthday calendar so every child's real day is marked warmly through the year.

playing_exploring: Children play out the universal joy of a birthday and bring their own family's way of celebrating into it.
They host, decorate, sing and share their way through the celebration.
active_learning: Children set up and run their birthday parties together, seeing the whole celebration through.
creating_thinking: Children count and add candles and shares, and compare how different families and countries celebrate the same happy day.
